#4163. Petit Planet Preview: Living the Cozy Life

The latest major entry in HoYoverse's catalog sends us to distant planets. We explore the multiplayer mini-games and friendly neighbors and planet customizations at a recent event!

HoYoverse is well known for their free-to-play gacha experiences, telling surprisingly intricate stories all while compelling their player base to get their favorite characters. That looks to change in their latest entry, Petit Planet.

This is a big deviation from what we’ve become accustomed to when it comes to HoYoverse, as while aspects to the overall formula remain, a lot of it has been modified to accommodate a cozier experience. This is all about building a life on a small planet with all your friends, be them NPCs or those online.

We were invited out to talk to the developers a couple of weeks ago and play a newly updated build of Petit Planet, and we couldn’t have had a cozier experience.

Before getting into anything, it should be said how much more of a multiplayer game this is compared to any of the other HoYoverse games we’ve had in the past. Genshin Impact has multiplayer functionality, which somewhat carried into Honkai: Star Rail (which uses its events well for cooperative and competitive play), but Petit Planet looks to up it to another level.

This is supposed to resemble something like Animal Crossing, having players not only be able to visit each other, but interact with them to a great degree. You can send friend requests and then easily access their world, although the number of things to do there is contained. It’s going to the Grand Bazaar that really turns things up.

This is a social hub-like area where players can go and play games with one another. For example, there's a rhythm game four players compete in, along with an Uno type game. Each of these games have a maximum number of four players to utilize, although there are possibilities for more. Being that the game isn’t out, this likely will be the groundwork for even more mini-games to come.

Participating in this mini-games seem to give you a Jelly currency, which can then be exchanged from various vendors for emotes, some of which can be interacted with other players, and other articles of clothing.

Because this is a life sim, there will be several things to do in the world on a daily basis, especially given this is a free-to-play HoYoverse game. There are daily and weekly challenges that can be accomplished, from chopping down trees to interacting with the Neighbors, and each generate different types of currency.

Because this is a free-to-play experience, there are quite a few different curries you will be able to obtain through daily activities but of course spend with your hard-earned money. While this wasn’t in the build we had, there’s no denying that’s how the game will generate its income from. It will still allow players to do their daily and weekly activities to generate some of these currencies, ensuring you don’t have to swipe, but remember this is still a HoYoverse game at the end of the day.

As for what you’ll be able to participate in, there are various energy-spending activities, from gathering materials from around your world to catching bugs and sea life. All of this contributes to the overall progression, although we aren't entirely sure what the endgame will truly be.

This feels like a game where you can sit back and chill with friends, slowly building upon a world without much pressure or FOMO. Regardless, there are still things that can be done in the world to ensure for some sort of progression, but whether there's a true endgame is still up for debate.

This wouldn’t be a cozy game without NPCs that roam around the worlds, and Petit Planet has a bevy to see. We’ve already been introduced to a number of the cute and cuddly cast in the past, but there’s even more we got to see in the latest demo. Each neighbor has their own function for why they are in your world, but mainly it’s for you to build and expand upon the relationships.

The Neighbors come with their own progress tree, going up three levels and seemingly able to go down if you neglect them. You'll be able to bring them onto your planet and set up little houses for them, and that’s not all. They'll have their own stories and journeys to go through from meeting them, talking them over time and giving them gifts, unlocking various moments with them.

By obtaining Footprints and the other currencies in Petit Planet, you'll be able to exchange them for various in-game cosmetics, such as clothing, which include facial wear and full outfits, and various placeable items.

Making sure your home is homey is key to immersing yourself into the Petit Planet system, as there are numerous options to choose from when building your perfect little abode. Whether it’s the furniture, the appliances or simply the wallpaper, there’s a staggering number of customizable options.

On top of that, building out your planet itself is just as important, as setting up roads to your neighbors and modifying the different accessories are put around things such as gardens lets you do so much more. It’s your personal little place you want to call home, even though the chilly planet we got to play on is relatively small. Here’s hoping there’s ways to expand upon it.

Petit Planet will be out by the end of the year on December 4 for PC and Mobile devices, with a Nintendo Switch 2 launch sometime in 2027.

#4162. Infinity Nikki ushers in the Year of the Horse with... a deer-themed Version 2.2

Chromatic Beings Everbright, the latest major Infinity Nikki update, has arrived, bringing Chinese New Year celebrations vibe to the game.

Infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, open-world dress-up RPG, has delivered yet another big content drop in the form of Chromatic Beings Everbright. The latest update brings the game up to version 2.2, and introduces a new narrative chapter, and gameplay taking place around a festival narrative.

If you couldn’t guess already, the new theme is Bloom Festival, inspired by Chinese New Year celebrations.

The big new story chapter takes place in the Infinity Nikki’s Wanxiang Realm. This deceptively serene and blissful region hides a dark secret, however. Chromafaces, the mythical inhabitants of the realm, have to embody fixed identities that dictate how they live and work.

These are doled out through Character Tokens, which are used to assign roles to each individual. The story follows Nikki as she uncovers the script that runs the realm and the facade it props up. Nikki will help free Chromafaces and dispel the illusion.

The Wanxiang Realm is split into three areas. Cai Ye is your typical lantern-lit district, where festivals and fireworks happen. Kongming Gorge is almost the opposite of that; a quiet and cold place. Finally, Jiuhua Pavilion literally floats above the region, and it's home to neverending music and dance.

The other big addition in 2.2 are the two new 5-Star Resonance Outfits with some interesting gameplay implications. Where Wanxiang Weaves Life is inspired by wuxia aesthetics, and true to its inspirations, it lets Nikki shapeshift into different Spirit Personas - and automatically collect resources in her vicinity.

Chroma's Mortal Heart, on the other hand, allows Nikki to fly around the Wanxiang Realm, drawing on the power of the Celestial Deer. This outfit also uses Celestial Deer Vision to automatically ping and mark treasure chests around her.

You can also look forward to Nefarious Shadows, a new Ability Outfit, which lets Nikki see through disguises, and reveals hidden paths in the world.

As with every major update, of course, there are themed activities and limited-time events throughout. Hotpot House is a cooking minigame where you attempt to run the eponymous restaurant, whereas Flavor Frenzy is series of platforming challenges that tasks you with gathering ingredients. Fortune Mahjong is a little more straightforward, with support for solo and multiplayer play.

#4159. T1 brings TenZ out of retirement a day after re-signing crashies from Fnatic

T1 has added two-time Masters champion Tyson 'TenZ' Ngo to its Valorant roster for VCT Pacific in 2027. The move ends his retirement and builds on T1's signing of crashies, who has just left London-based Fnatic.

T1 has ended Tyson ‘TenZ’ Ngo’s retirement. The organisation confirmed on 12 November that he will join its Valorant roster for VCT Pacific in 2027. It made the announcement with a post and a welcome video.

T1 called him a ‘living legend’ of Valorant. It said he was starting a new chapter with the organisation.

TenZ retired from professional play in 2024. He has spent this year at T1 as a content creator. The announcement moves him from that role into the competitive squad.

His record explains the attention. With Sentinels, he beat Fnatic 3-0 in the Masters Reykjavík 2021 final. He then won Masters Madrid 2024 with a 3-2 win over Gen.G. That made him the first Americas player to win more than one VCT Masters event, Liquipedia records.

The TenZ news came a day after T1 confirmed Austin ‘crashies’ Roberts. He returns six years after T1 released him in September 2020. crashies called T1 the place ‘where it all started’. He said he was excited for the new challenge.

He played for Fnatic from 11 December 2024 until 4 November 2026. He joined T1 on 11 November 2026.

His exit is part of a wider reshuffle at the London-based organisation. Fnatic lost the Masters Toronto 2025 grand final 3-1 to Paper Rex. It then lost the Valorant Champions 2025 grand final in Paris 3-2 to NRG. On 2 November, Fnatic released head coach Andrey ‘ENGH’ Sholokhov. It said it was making changes ahead of the 2027 season.

T1 has also kept some continuity. It extended BuZz’s contract on 6 November 2026. The new deal runs until the end of 2028.

The VCT structure for 2027 was announced on 28 October. Under it, the eight Pacific partner teams go straight into Kickoff in January 2027. The other four Kickoff places go to teams from regional open qualifiers.

The KING is back! 👑A living legend of VALORANT, 'TenZ' begins a new chapter with T1.Ready to make history under the red wings, join us in giving him a warm welcome!

📺 https://t.co/ny3VtTtYnx#T1VALORANT pic.twitter.com/gmgLEzXJR2

Before Kickoff, T1 has a date in Los Angeles. It is one of six teams directly invited to Red Bull Home Ground 2026. Fnatic, Sentinels, G2 Esports, NRG and ZETA DIVISION have also been invited. That puts the former clubs of both TenZ and crashies in the same field as T1.

The event runs from 10 to 13 December. Group stage matches are on 10 and 11 December. Bracket play and the semi-finals follow on 12 December. The grand final is on 13 December.

#4156. Zenelss Zone Zero Version 2.6 has you playing as an event planner and social media manager for an idol group

Zenelss Zone Zero's Encore for an Old Dream has a good excuse for introducing some new mechanics to the action game.

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program has delivered a tonne of information about the game’s big upcoming update, Version 2.6. This latest addition kicks off celebrations in New Eridu, and it’s dubbed Encore for an Old Dream.

Version 2.6 is not far off, either, arriving in ZZZ on February 6 - exactly one week from today. Encore for an Old Dream is something of an in-between story that takes place after the end of Season 2.

The narrative of 2.6 sees the Proxies’ return to Sixth Street for New Eridu's annual Gilded Carrot Day. At the centre of the celebrations is the debut of idol group Angels of Delusion at the 404 Error music venue, but not all is as it seems.

The story follows the Proxies getting invited backstage to support the group, which also includes helping them set up practice schedules, organise events and manage social media activities. There’s a rhythm minigame as part of that, along with new maps and mechanics for Marcel Adventure.

Angels of Delusion is also the group that the two new Agents being introduced in this update belong to. Members of the same group are capable of performing coordinated attacks. The new arrivals are Sunna and Aria.

Sunna is a an S-Rank Physical Support Agent who specialises in boosting teammates using Attack and Anomaly. Her Ultimate sees her pull out a giant hammer to land heavy damage, and bring teammates into combat using Quick Assist. Sunna’s companion, Bubblegum, can cast Cat's Gaze on enemies, marking them for detonation. Bubblegum can also buff the squad’s attack.

Aria is the other new arrival, the group’s lead vocalist who can shift between two forms, idol projection and construct. Aria is an Ether Anomaly Agent who also deals high burst damage, specifically against enemies who suffer from any Attribute Anomalies.

Sunna and Aria also benefit from the support of the amusingly named Bangboo Biggest Fan, a fan club president who can heal them over time, and boost the squad’s Attack any time two or more Angels of Delusion members are present.

Version 2.6’s S-Rank re-runs are Yixuan (Auric Ink - Rupture), and Yuzuha (Physical - Support), who you can look forward to as part of the banners.

Version 2.6 will also expand Hollow Zero with a new game mode, Operation Matrix. The mode offers themed stages that rotate weekly, each offering new mechanics. You can now also Sweep in Hollow Zero.

Beyond all the celebrations, this update also brings combat kit overhauls to a couple of older S-Rank characters, Lycaon and Harumasa. You can look forward to multiple limited-time events, too, including one where you can earn a new outfit for Pan Yinhu.

The big event is naturally going to be themed around Gilded Carrot Day, and it actually starts today. There’s the usual run of login rewards (about 3,300 Polychromes), as well as daily activities. Yet another login event - Gilded Surprise, Wonderful Boo-ns - will be available February 14-23, offering daily draws from a pool of 4 billion Polychrome.

#4155. Starsand Island is a life and farming sim that isn't gacha, and it's out next week

Starsand Island officially has an Early Access release date, and it sounds like it won't stay there for years.

Though it may seem like we just had a big life sim release in Heartopia, 2026 actually has more than one highly-anticipated release in that particular subgenre of cozy game. The next big one on the horizon is Starsand Island, the life and farming sim from Seed Sparkle Lab.

The game has been gaining momentum since the launch of a demo in October last year, but the developer never quite managed to commit to a date for its debut title. Until now.

Seed Sparkle Lab announced today that Starsand Island will enter Early Access on February 11, which is only a bit over one week from now. This goes for Steam and the Xbox Preview Program version.

The developer said to expect a fairly short Early Access run, as the full launch is expected in the summer of this year. When the full release arrives, the game will also make the jump to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series, as well as Switch 2.

The full release is also expected to bring Steam Deck support and introduce the multiplayer mode, which will not be available during Early Access

Starsand Island has something of a unique look compared to other games in the subgenre. The storybook, anime-inspired aesthetics are popular in the realm of gacha games, of course. However, seeing as this particular game isn’t gacha, being a premium product means it’s going to offer something free-to-play games aren’t designed to.

Speaking of which, the game will be available in two editions: Standard and Deluxe, with the latter including Romanticism-inspired outfits, furniture, and other customisation items. If you buy either during launch, you’ll also get a Chinese New Year bonus with even more outfits and furniture.

On top of the usual systems of farming, mining, and making friends with adorable characters (and animals), the game also has combat that pits you against ancient guardians. You can, of course, also build a home in it, and decorate it to your heart's content.

Seed Sparkle Lab says you can expect about 100 hours of content in the Early Access launch build, and more features will arrive over the course of the next six or so months, including a crossover event with My Time At Portia.

You can look forward to more Starsand Island coverage from us in the near future. Until then, you can get started by planning who you’re going to date now.

#4154. Dota 2 returns to Esports World Cup 2027 as PARIVISION chase a first repeat title

Dota 2 will return to the Riyadh-hosted Esports World Cup in 2027, though dates, format and prize money are still to come. The title has never been won twice, and its prize pool has fallen at every edition so far.

Dota 2’s place at Esports World Cup 2027 was announced without dates, a prize pool, a format or any invited teams. The whole event is listed for July to August 2027.

The 2026 tournament had originally been planned for Riyadh before it was moved to Paris on 20 May 2026.

The first edition, Riyadh Masters 2024, carried a US$5,000,000 prize pool. In 2025 Team Spirit took US$1,000,000 from a US$3,000,000 pool in a 16-team event. The 2026 tournament ran from 7 to 19 July with 24 teams. That field was eight teams larger than a year earlier.

The winner still takes a large share. PARIVISION collected US$750,000, or 37.5% of the pool, plus 1,000 Club Championship points. Runners-up BetBoom Team received US$340,000 and 750 points, Liquipedia reported.

Those points feed into a larger prize. In 2026 the Club Championship paid US$30 million across the top 24 clubs. The champion club received US$7 million from an overall event prize pool of US$75 million. AG.AL won it with 5,300 points, stopping Team Falcons from winning a third title in a row. For organisations weighing the cost of a Dota 2 roster, that club prize is part of the calculation.

Not every club is staying. Falcons released all five players from the roster that won The International 2025, according to Timesaver.gg.

No club or player has won the event’s Dota 2 title more than once. Each of the three editions went to a different club with a different roster. Gaimin Gladiators beat Team Liquid in the 2024 final. A year later, Team Spirit swept Team Falcons 3-0. As the 2026 champions, PARIVISION now get the first chance to defend the title.

PVISION are your Dota 2 at EWC26 Champions! 👏 pic.twitter.com/34U67Oaj7G

— Esports World Cup (@EWC_EN) July 20, 2026

Their rivals arrive in form. Team Spirit went out of the 2026 event before the final. A month later, they won The International 2026 in Shanghai. Yatoro and Collapse became the first players to win three Internationals. Team Yandex finished third at both the 2026 Esports World Cup and The International. After signing ATF, they won PGL Wallachia Season 9 and BLAST SLAM VIII.

The route into the event is taking shape. The organiser’s Road to EWC qualifier programme for 2027 aims to involve 1.8 million players across more than 400 events. Qualifier slots for each game will be announced later. Counter-Strike 2, already confirmed for both 2027 and 2028, will hold a 32-team event in Riyadh from 20 July to 1 August 2027.

#4152. 10 Game Boy Advance Metroidvanias That Respect Your Time

Josh Speer has been writing about games for more than a decade, and has been a fan his entire life, since getting his NES.

The Game Boy Advance marked the beginning of the Metroidvania genre as a respected and more commonplace one. Not only were there many great games that were released on the handheld, but developers took some real chances to expand it in unusual ways.

Partly because of the genre, and partly because of being on a handheld, all the Metroidvanias on this list are ones that do a good job of respecting your time. That means they're relatively short burns and that they're pretty streamlined.

Metroidvanias can take a long time to get through, but these ones deliver all the punch of a long game in a package that fits your life.

There's a wide variety of games here too, some well known titles, others more eclectic. No matter what, though, they're all great and fun little Metroidvanias which do a good job of respecting us gamers. So join me as we return to a wonderful handheld that I truly adored.

Back in its heyday, Cartoon Network had a lot of amazing shows, but one of the best was Samurai Jack. And even though I don't typically enjoy adaptations of those programs to videogames, they did a surprisingly good job with Samurai Jack: The Amulet of Time.

Not only did it feature everyone's favorite samurai, but it also has him hopping through time to procure fragments of elemental gems. Eventually they'll allow Jack to return to his own time period, but in the short term, they unlock new powers, such as a battle hammer and super jump.

While Samurai Jack: The Amulet of Time features great visual style and is a fun time, it's also more than a bit derivative of better examples of the genre. Still, for fans of Samurai Jack, this is an excellent adventure.

As a big fan of Spooky month, I adore The Nightmare Before Christmas. But as iconic as the movie is, many of the video game adaptations have been less than stellar. Probably the best example was on the Game Boy Advance in an adventure called Tim Burton's The Nightmare Before Christmas: The Pumpkin King.

The game serves as a prequel to the movie, and showcases how Jack Skellington became the Pumpkin King. There's all sorts of crazy, including a bug infestation, as well as the the schemes of Oogie Boogie to become top dog.

As for how it plays, it's more of a platformer than a full throated Metroidvania, but it's just enough of an example to include it here. Jack gets new powers and upgrades as it proceeds, there's challenging boss battles and the like. Combined with a really vibrant visual style, this is one handheld Metroidvania that's worth your time.

Everyone looks to The Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown for when the series finally embraced Metroidvanias. But it actually happened much, much earlier on the GBA in Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time. And while the game had multiple console releases, the handheld one did the best job of embracing the genre years before The Lost Crown.

The GBA game has you running around the palace of Azad in 2D, fighting baddies and saving citizens. You'll get new powers, rewind time itself, and get powerful upgrades for helping out the people of Persia.

Most interesting, you'll also switch between the prince and another playable character named Farah. Which isn't that common in the genre, but it makes sense thematically and helps this relatively basic Metroidvania stand apart.

When most of us think about Konami and Metroidvanias, we naturally think about Castlevania. But they actually tried their hand with other series, including Shaman King. The massively popular manga turned out to be a pretty fun little Metroidvania in Shaman King: Master of Spirits.

What's wild about it is that you can equip a variety of different spirits, both with passive and active abilities. Meaning that it plays out a lot like Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow and Dawn of Sorrow, as well as Order of Ecclesia.

You'll get spirits by doing all sorts of things, and can even equip different decks of them that you can swap between on the fly. While it's fun and visually attractive, this is also a pretty basic Metroidvania which you can beat in 10 hours or less.

Unlike the other games on this list, Shantae Advance: Risky Revolution has one unique characteristic – it came out in 2025 for GBA as well as other consoles. WayForward had always wanted to make this adventure, and finally found an excuse when Limited Run agreed to partner with them for physical releases.

The game takes place between the original game and Risky's Revenge, meaning that our favorite genie girl can still transform into a variety of animal forms. Those include classics like monkey and elephant, as well as stranger ones like spider and harpy. Each of them provides new ways to explore, as well as unique ways to attack.

The biggest throwback aspect of this adventure is using Tremor Engines to shuffle around the position of the background, allowing Shantae to find new paths forward. Throw in a short run time, fun multiplayer mode, tons of humor and some challenging boss battles, and this is one amazing Metroidvania adventure.

Fans of the PS2 console probably need to check out this list of poorly known Metroidvanias worth playing on the system.

Sometimes I think about what could have been, and one off games that should have been the beginning of a legacy. One of those games was Scurge: Hive. It was released on both GBA and Nintendo DS, but I played it on the older system, and was utterly bewitched by it.

Jenosa is afflicted by the parasitic Scurge, and has to not only face the horrible mutations it wreaks on planet Inos, but on her as well. You're constantly racing against the clock, and eventually even have to face the infection inside you. Along the way, you'll get upgrades and fun new mechanics like a mechanical grapple.

While most Metroidvanias play better in 2D, I found the isometric style worked very well in Scurge: Hive. Mix that with elemental weapons and a paper/rock/scissors system, and it's very addictive. It's also quite short, as you can beat the game in a little more than 10 hours.

I'll acknowledge that Drill Dozer is a hard game to narrow down stylistically. It features lots of platforming, intense boss battles, unique upgrades and a very powerful drill mech. But given that it's also one of the best games on the GBA, I felt worth highlighting it here, even if it's not a traditional Metroidvania.

You'll use the shoulder buttons to control the direction that you drill, and it can do more than just burst forward. Jill can use her Dozer to unscrew bolts, destroying blocks and fighting enemies. You'll even get upgrades that let it traverse watery sections and fly through the air.

It's pretty rare for any game to stay with me for more than a decade or so, which is part of why I had to include Drill Dozer on this list. I haven't forgotten it since I played it more than two decades ago, and I still fervently hope that somehow this amazing adventure gets a modern follow up.

Inti Creates wasn't on my radar until I played the first Mega Man Zero. A wholly original, super challenging take on the series that bridged the gap between the X and Legends series. And while this is still a platformer, it also features a mission-based system and the ability to level up your gear.

Better yet, beating some bosses provides elemental chips that allows Zero customize his attacks. Then there's Cyber Elves, which are hard to find but vital upgrades that are also single use. Finding them can drastically change how you play the game, meaning that purists would go out of their way not to overuse them.

One thing that also helped distinguish Mega Man Zero from earlier entries was how brutally hard it was, especially the boss battles. The series did start to tone things down in latter entries, but not enough you could call any of the series easy. A really remarkably different Metroidvania.

Hot on the heels of Castlevania: Symphony of the Night, we got Circle of the Moon. A game that was more of a classic example of the series than a pure Metroidvania. It was also incredibly dark and hard to see. Which is why it was a brilliant move on Koji Igarashi's part to make the next game, Harmony of Dissonance, a bright, bold festival of color.

Even though it's a GBA game, Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance is a beautiful game that still holds up today. It features Juste Belmont, who is capable of powerful magical attacks by fusing sub weapons with magical books. And while that's a lot of fun, it also makes this one of the easiest of the Igavanias.

Still, this is a very fun Metroidvania that features some surprising boss battles and a fascinating premise. But if you know what you're doing, it's also one you can easily beat in 8 hours or less, at least once you figure out the convoluted maps.

After Super Metroid's success, Nintendo could have played it safe. Instead, they gave us one of the best games in the series on the GBA in Metroid Fusion. Sure, it's linear and thus pretty short. But it also was the first game in the series to really embrace a coherent narrative. It also injected a bit of survival horror into the series, a trend that was later embraced in Metroid Dread.

The X-Parasites brought a lot of terror into the adventure, and totally changed how Samus fought back. So much so that she had to get a brand new suit, which makes her stronger but also more susceptible to cold. Like other games in the series, beating bosses will provide powerful new upgrades, which you'll need to deal with the deadly doppelganger called SA-X.

This isn't just a great Metroidvania you can beat in less than 10 hours. It's an amazing handheld adventure that's just as fun today as before, and it efficiently laid the groundwork for the series to evolve in exciting ways, including the upcoming Metroid Ravenous.

If you're looking for unexplored gems in video games, I recommend these ten Metroidvanias that are unexpected masterpieces.

#4151. Grand Theft Auto VI Will Run At 30 FPS On All Consoles, But PS5 Pro Will Feature 'Improved Clarity' And Ray-Traced Shadows

Grand Theft Auto VI launches next week on Thursday, November 19, and you can preload the game on your PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S starting today, Rockstar Games has announced. The studio has also revealed what kind of visuals players can expect on their respective consoles, making clear that regardless of where you play, GTA VI targets 30 FPS gameplay.

"Grand Theft Auto VI has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits to bring the vast and rich world of Leonida to life – while maintaining the density and visual fidelity of all its environments and inhabitants," Rockstar writes in a blog post.

Rockstar Games also breaks down the different graphical settings available on PlayStation and Xbox consoles. On PS5 Pro, GTA VI will feature "improved clarity through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and ray-traced shadows only available on PlayStation 5 Pro." On PS5 and PS5 Pro, the game will include "high-fidelity haptic feedback" fully integrated into DualSense controllers and adjustable via accessibility settings, improved spatial rendering so all in-game sounds take full advantage of Tempest 3D audio, and improved load times, "making Grand Theft Auto VI play best on PlayStation 5 consoles."

On Xbox consoles, Rockstar doesn't dive into performance; instead, it focuses on Xbox Cloud Gaming on Xbox Series X/S and Xbox One consoles, noting this feature will use Xbox Series S graphics settings.

GTA VI will also fully support Remote Play on PlayStation and Xbox.

GTA VI launches November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S.

For more, check out the song "Pusher" from the game's original score, then check out the GTA VI launch trailer. After that, check out this exclusive story about how GTA VI features over 170 animal species and another about its tropical storms and hurricanes.

#4150. Nioh 3 launches, immediately becomes the most played Nioh ever on Steam

Just a few hours after launch, Nioh 3 is already the biggest release in series history on Steam.

It sounds like Koei Tecmo’s decision to finally release a Nioh game on PC day-and-date with PlayStation has paid off. The highly-anticipated Nioh 3 has gone live across both platforms, a first for a series that typically spends its initial release months as a console exclusive.

On Steam, and despite having only been available for just a few hours, the game has broken series records, and it continues to climb.

At the time of writing, Nioh 3 has peaked at 42,822 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), and the number keeps going up. Because it’s in the middle of day in Europe and everyone is at work, it’s entirely possible - if not likely - that this figure will get much higher. A weekend bump is also possible, as we’ve seen with several recent releases.

As it stands, the current peak concurrent is enough to get the game in Steam’s top 20 most played games.

This already puts it ahead of all other Nioh games on Steam. The original Nioh peaked at 10,649 when it released in November, 2017. Nioh 2 fared much better, peaking at 41,325 concurrent players in February, 2021.

Of course, you could see that success coming a mile away. The game is currently number one worldwide in Steam’s list of top sellers. This is a jump of 46 positions, for a total of three weeks Nioh 3 has spent in that list.

There are many reasons as to why Nioh 3 has done as well as it has. Word of mouth coming off last year’s PS5-exclusive demo, and the more positive coverage that followed since are just two.

Just last week, Team Ninja released a pretty generous demo across both platforms, which has been well received by players, and likely contributed to sales, in no small part because progress in the demo carries over to the full game.

Critical reviews have been incredibly positive, too. We awarded the game four out of five stars, calling it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.” It will be interesting to see what number the highest peak concurrent actually settles on over the weekend.

If you're excited about the game, you will probably want to go ahead and do this because it will take up a whopping 212 GB of space on your drives – make the room now so you don't hit this roadblock next week when the game goes live on Thursday, November 19.

The blog post also details performance on PlayStation and Xbox consoles, and you can read more about what to expect here.

We're just over two weeks away from the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, which recently graced the cover of Game Informer. Ahead of its November 19 launch, Rockstar Games has announced that digital preloading for GTA VI will begin next week on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

More specifically, preloading on Xbox Series X/S will begin Tuesday, November 10, at 12 a.m. GMT (4 p.m. PT/7 p.m. ET on November 9), and on PS5 at midnight local time in your time zone. Although Rockstar isn't producing physical discs of GTA VI, you can still buy a physical box at retail, which includes a download code for the game. The studio says, "Code-in-box versions for both consoles should be available from retailers beginning November 12."

The preload file will require 212 GB on your device, so make sure you have the space before you start the download. You can find more details about this process here.

Elsewhere in today's GTA VI news, Rockstar has revealed that on November 19, it will add an official printable GTA VI cover art poster and a map of Leonida as a free digital download to the game's official site. GTA VI launches November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S.

#4147. MSI 2027 heads to Valencia as Riot reshapes Split 1 with First Stand: All In in China

Riot will take the Mid-Season Invitational to Spain in 2027, bringing a top-tier League of Legends event back to Europe for the first time since the Worlds 2024 final in London. Its one-off, expanded First Stand in China will also change Split 1 for the LEC, with the full details due in January.

Europe will host a top-tier League of Legends event again in 2027. Riot set out its international calendar on 13 November, the eve of the Worlds 2026 final. The Mid-Season Invitational goes to Valencia. London’s staging of the Worlds 2024 final was the last time the continent held an international League of Legends tournament.

For British fans, that puts a top-tier event within Europe next year. Riot has not yet given dates or ticket details for the Feria de Valencia event.

Spain’s last international League of Legends event came in 2019. That year, Madrid’s Palacio Vistalegre staged the Worlds quarter-finals and semi-finals. Valencia has never hosted one before.

China will stage First Stand: All In at the start of the 2027 season. Riot calls this single edition its largest tournament ever.

First Stand 2027 had originally been given to Southeast Asia. The bigger format took it to China instead. Southeast Asia will now host the event in 2028.

The change reaches every regional league, including the LEC. The larger event will change Split 1, just as Fnatic, G2 and the other LEC teams rebuild their rosters. In 2026, First Stand ran from 16 to 22 March, between the two regional splits. A bigger event at the start of the year leaves less certainty about how that window will look in 2027.

Riot has not yet said how many teams will take part or how they will qualify. Until then, LEC teams are building squads without knowing how many European places are on offer.

Worlds 2027 will be shared between two countries. The Swiss Stage goes to Nagoya, Japan. The quarter-finals and semi-finals move to the Suwon Convention Center in South Korea. The title decider goes to Seoul Arena, which is still under construction.

The arena was 81% built on 23 October. Work is due to finish in May 2027, with the venue opening in June 2027.

The city is backing the event with public money. Seoul has set aside 1.369 billion won (about US$1.02 million) in its proposed 2027 budget to host the Worlds final and Fan Fest, Sheep Esports reported.

#4146. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.0 brings a new world, and a Fortnite collaboration

Honkai: Star Rail's next major update introduces a whole new planet to the RPG, and way more besides.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

The upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the big new world headlining Version 4.0.

Planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

The squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

The imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

The Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

Much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

As you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Version 4.0 introduces two new 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

General Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

Her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

The other new arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

When you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

Version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

If you log in after launch, you’ll get 20 free pulls and a new free outfit for Ruan Mei. If you play while the Yao Guang fortune event is active, you could earn 1,600 Stellar Jades. You can also expect a free 5-Star character selector to arrive at some point after launch, giving you a free choice between popular (but admittedly a bit old for the meta these days) limited-banner characters Jing Yuan, Kafka, Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae, Jingliu, Sparkle, Acheron, and Aventurine.

Finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the new outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

If you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be announced at a later date.

#4145. 10 Best Romance Anime Where Falling in Love is the Easy Part

Usama Mehmood is a Senior Writer at DualShockers with more than five years of experience in the video game industry. He has been writing professionally since 2021 and covering games since 2022, with work spanning guides, lists, reviews, and features across action-adventure games, JRPGs, open-world titles, racing games,

The romance genre in anime is evidently meaningful and important to countless fans, myself included. From obsessively reading Horimiya (better than the butchered anime) to bawling my eyes out at the peak that was Clannad and then its After Story.Most romance anime also have a habit of making falling in love look like the hardest part of a relationship. After several episodes of awkward encounters, stolen glances, misunderstandings, and finally working up the courage to confess, you'd think the two lovebirds had overcome their biggest obstacle.

If you're tired of dumb misunderstandings and love polyhedrons, here are some Romance Anime for People Who Hate Cheap Drama.

However, the real work begins after that phase. You see, feelings can be mutual, but that doesn't mean two people automatically know how to navigate each other's insecurities, conflicting personalities, or the unexpected challenges that life throws their way. Thankfully, some romance anime understand that there's considerably more to love than the excitement of a first confession.So, armed with my extensive cult following of this genre since my teenage years, here are the best romance anime where falling in love is the easy part, from one-off slice-of-life seasonals to the more emotionally demanding dramedies.

For all my fellow video gamers, I thought I’d reel you in with My Love Story with Yamada-kun at Lv999. Getting over a breakup is never easy; I can attest to that, but Akane Kinoshita definitely wasn't expecting to find her next romantic interest through an online RPG.After discovering that her bf has been cheating on her, she meets Akito Yamada, a notoriously indifferent MMO gamer who initially seems uninterested in anything outside his favourite hobby. Their clashing personalities couldn't be more different, but their friendship gradually develops into something considerably more meaningful.

It’s a 13-episode show that beautifully explores emotional maturity and the importance of understanding another person rather than simply expecting them to reciprocate your feelings. The only downside I have to mention is that the anime doesn’t fully cover the story, so you might need to binge the manga to get the full experience here.

As someone who originally read the manga on and off on his phone, “I Have a Crush at Work” (2025) stayed on my radar as soon as I heard it was in production. Workplace romances are complicated enough without having to pretend you're not dating the person sitting a few desks away.But then you have these two coworkers, Yui Mitsuya and Masugu Tateishi, who start a relationship but decide to keep it secret from their colleagues. That arrangement, in turn, creates an amusing contrast between their professional behaviour and how they act together when nobody is around them.

Fair warning: It’s a little more comedy-based, but beneath that layer, the show neatly tackles a relatable problem: how do you maintain a healthy relationship when you spend so much of your day together, yet can't openly acknowledge it? And that’s exactly where this show will make you adore it wholeheartedly.

We’re keeping the Workplace Romance streak going, and this is the perfect time to give some appreciation to one of my and everyone else’s all-time favorites in this sub-genre of romance anime: Wotakoi.I genuinely think it needs little introduction, given how widely popular it is, whether it's the show or even the web manga. Two adults who are hopeless romantics in theory, but who actually have absolutely no idea how to navigate an actual relationship? This show literally answers that question with childhood friends, Narumi and Hirotaka.

And not just them; you also get a healthy dose of screen time with their respective co-workers, and if I’m being honest, I may slightly prefer Hanako and Kabakura’s cute moments to the two main characters. But again, we’re in a similar problem where the anime and OVAs don’t fully adapt everything, so either go read it or, like me, hopelessly wait for a follow-up season.

Like what My Happy Marriage has to offer? Well, here are some of the best shows that feature somewhat of a similar theme.

This next one’s from my nostalgic vault because, like Wotakoi, Golden Time is a popular romcom anime that’s beloved by (almost) everyone. You’ve got a fairly simple premise at the beginning: our MC, Banri Tada, is settling into college life when Kouko barges in, and the two fall for each other quickly.And that’s the easy part. The bigger elephant in the room is that Banri has lost the memories of his hometown and past after an accident, and the real kicker is what that gap does to a relationship once the honeymoon glow wears off.

What I like is how mature the drama feels between these two characters and the rest of the cast, especially at a time when I thought all romance anime felt the same, with their usual high school settings. The show obviously isn’t a masterpiece or anything, but if you want an anime where the feelings are the easy part and the baggage drives most of the plot, it’s worth the 24 episodes.

We’re taking things old-school here, back to the golden age of the late 2000s, when the shoujo series Itazura na Kiss aired. Look, a lot of romance anime are happy to wrap things up once the two leads finally get together, but this show gives you a broader look than your typical lovey-dovey couple story.It follows Kotoko and Naoki from their school days into adulthood, showing how their relationship changes as they navigate college, marriage, and just life in general beyond their adolescence.

Now, given that it is based on a 1990s Shoujo, Naoki’s behavior and character may be slightly concerning, but trust me, the show is genuinely a wholesome treat, especially when these two start living under one roof, getting through their daily frictions of life, and then eventually build a family together.

TONIKAWA, or rather, as I prefer to call it, Tonikaku Kawaii, is easily one of the sweetest romcoms I had the pleasure of reading long before the seasonal anime adaptation premiered.What’s so great here is how the show totally skips the confession part: Nasa meets Tsukasa, falls for her, and they then get married very early in the story. From there, the series focuses on the joys and growing pains of newlywed life, as the pair learn more about each other while adjusting to living together.

It's honestly a bit more lighthearted than you’d expect from the other entries I’ve mentioned here, but oh man, I’d be lying if I didn’t mention how almost every single moment of these two puts a gigantic smile on your face. Apologies in advance to any hopeless romantics out there, but trust me, this show is a massive ball of sunshine to help cheer you up.

Falling in love for the first time is one thing, but then figuring out how to make that relationship work is an entirely different challenge.It’s a universal experience almost all of us go through when we’re young and full of these different aspirations. Yet Tsuki ga Kirei captures that awkward transition beautifully through Kotaro Azumi, an aspiring novelist, and Akane Mizuno, a track-and-field enthusiast, who grow closer during their final year of middle school.

Their relationship begins with these little tender yet familiar moments, but the show doesn't treat getting together as the finish line. Instead, it explores everything that comes afterward with jealousy, parental expectations, and the looming uncertainty of moving on to high school. It's a sincere coming-of-age romance that understands exactly why staying together can be harder than falling in love.

These 7 romance anime capture the quiet moments that linger long after the credits roll, perfect for when your heart needs a little extra love

My days of avidly consuming manga or watching almost every interesting anime in my piled-up backlog on MAL/Kitsu are long gone, but when a show like “You and I Are Polar Opposites” comes along, it instantly reminds you why this medium is still alive and kicking for you.It quite literally lives up to the title: on one hand, you have Suzuki, an energetic and sociable high school girl; on the other, you have Tani, her quiet, straightforward classmate who’s just the epitome of the silent-treatment energy at first glance. Despite their contrasting personalities, they develop feelings for each other and eventually take the plunge, starting a relationship.

And it’s not just about them; you get to see their everyday lives grow together alongside their wildcard cast of friends/classmates. It has those high school romcom tropes going for it, but trust me when I say the writing and character dramedy are exceptionally well done, and almost every episode feels like a joy to watch, with no filler.

Nana is one of my favorite anime and manga series of all time. I’ve got Nana Osaki as my avatar across most of my socials, and it's mainly because of how much this show means to me. What starts as a story about two young women navigating life in Tokyo slowly becomes one of the most emotionally complex explorations of love, friendship, and heartbreak I've ever experienced.

The series doesn't romanticize the idea of finding someone and living happily ever after; instead, it showcases two bittersweet parallels: Hachi's search for affection and stability, which often leads her into situations that make her question her own worth, while Nana's fiercely independent exterior hides a vulnerability she struggles to confront.I sometimes obsess over Ai Yazawa's writing in this series because nobody feels entirely innocent or irredeemable; almost all of these flawed young adults make messy decisions, hurt people they care about, and occasionally sabotage their own happiness.

To some of you reading, I hope you can relate to me on one thing: there’s some media you just can’t revisit with all earnestness because it’s left an emotional scar.That’s exactly what Clannad: After Story did to me, and I both love and hate it for doing that. While the original Clannad does a wonderful job establishing Okazaki and Nagisa's relationship, After Story takes things several steps further by exploring what happens once the sunshine of adolescence is over. It’s also where the show takes a full-blown descent into heartbreak.

The two are no longer simply teenagers; they're young adults trying to figure out what it means to build a life together. Marriage, parenthood, financial struggles, grief, and letting go. That one entire episode dedicated to Okazaki realizing and forgiving his Father has absolutely scarred my heart.The overall show and the OG VN are important to a lot of fans in the medium, almost being iconic for how the story beats were presented in it, like a train wreck. It's a bittersweet yet painfully gut-wrenching narrative, and one I still find hard to revisit without getting a lump in my throat.

Love isn’t always simple, but these 7 best romance anime on Crunchyroll capture its magic, heartbreak, and everything in between.

#4143. House House Discloses AI Use For 'Under 0.1%' Of Big Walk's Code Following IGF Voting Controversy

Big Walk developer House House has found itself at the center of a controversy over the upcoming Independent Games Festival on March 3, 2027, after a group of its jurors said they would not vote for any game that has used generative AI in any capacity. The jurors' statement does not name House House or Big Walk, but the studio eventually updated its FAQ to explain how it used generative AI for coding after IGF discussions. After vaguely posting on social media, those associated with IGF made clear that a sticking point in the voting process was Big Walk.

Former games journalist and game developer Austin Walker posted the IGF jurors' statement on Bluesky, explaining that voting has been difficult this year due to the "significant increase in the number of submitted games developed with generative AI tools."

"This has set off some fairly intense discussion and disagreement across the judge and jury pools, and at this point there is no universal consensus on what (if anything) is to be done," the statement reads. "The IGF has affirmed that we may cast our votes according to our own tastes and values. But we, as a contingent of IGF jurors, feel that this trend and the games embracing it deserve stronger pushback than a vote in silence."

The statement continues, explaining that not all jurors are on board with the blanket statement, citing reasons including "their ability to safely sign without professional blowback." It continues, "Above all: Our goal is to state solidarity with those who despair over the future of their art, their craft, and their industry – including those who have experimented with these tools, but who now believe they are not in our best interest."

The statement continues with the jurors' beliefs regarding gen-AI, including its negative effects, that any gen-AI used in any process of game development is not okay, noting specifically that "AI-generated code is not an exception to these harms," and more.

"For those reasons, this year we are declining to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity," the statement says. "We urge the IGF to adopt a strong anti-AI policy for future years that disallows games containing any AI-generated work." The statement then includes the names of the IGF jurors who signed it.

Big Walk isn't specifically mentioned within that statement. However, Kyle LeClair, a four-time IGF judge and a juror for the upcoming IGF, tells Aftermath that "it got to the point where the most-discussed game this year almost entirely involved its AI usage, overshadowing pretty much everything else." LeClair says it felt like a boiling point, adding, "Anyhow, strong props to the jurors for taking this stance and putting out this letter as well, even if some people believe that using AI for coding purposes is a more gray area, we're at a point where the amount of AI slop clogging up the indie game scene means having to take hard stances such as this in order to discourage such an amount of recklessness."

Again, no mention of Big Walk. However, game developer Bruno Diaz took to BlueSky to confirm the speculation: that most-discussed game was Big Walk. "Okay, because the cat is out of the f---ing bag, I might as well combat misinformation a bit: 1. The reason IGF judges are aware of the LLM use in the development of Big Walk is through a disclosure shared by House House. 2. This disclosure was required by IGF rules. 3. While some have characterized the LLM usage as just fixing one individual blocking bug, this is a bit inaccurate; the description given by House House mentioned there being several instances, though they did also say it was mostly 'consultative' use and not code gen or agents."

Diaz notes that they believe that distinction is without a difference, adding that "to my knowledge, it is not the case that Big Walk is non-compliant with the former [Steam's AI disclosure requirements]."

"Yes, there was a large discussion about this in internal IGF forums," Diaz said. "Yes, a lot of people said things that I personally think were disingenuous, extremely disappointing, or just (frankly) dumb. No, I have no intention of talking about it in further detail or exposing anyone. [...] Ultimately, it is extremely difficult for a group of over 100 people to keep a secret so I expected this to come out eventually. Shrug emoji. If you think something is reputationally damaging, consider not doing it."

With discussion surrounding Big Walk happening during the IGF discussions, House House updated its FAQ to address, "Was AI used to make Big Walk?" Here's what the FAQ reads, in full:

"In the final stretch of Big Walk’s development, LLMs were used sparingly by House House to help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs. In some cases, snippets from LLM responses were copied as a starting point to be modified into game code—we’d estimate that well under 0.1% of Big Walk’s code had anything to do with this usage, and generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game.

The primary use case for House House’s use of LLMs was to research, via chatbots, issues we encountered with third-party code. If you’re technically-minded, and curious, here’s an example. We needed to cull shadow casters by distance from the camera, but Unity URP only allows culling shadow casters by distance in camera forwards, so shadow casters behind the player were being rendered at an infinite distance. This made our game run 50% slower for around 20 seconds at sunrise and sunset. We researched the problem extensively, and we looked at the URP code ourselves, but we couldn’t find a way. Then, we were able to speak directly to an engineer at Unity, who asked around and ultimately concluded that what we wanted wasn’t possible. Finally, we posed the question to an LLM chatbot. After a few dead ends, it suggested a possible fix, and while we had to modify the suggestion extensively, it worked. This fix represented about 10 lines of code inside URP.

We originally wrote a version of the above disclosure as it was a suggested part of our IGF submission. We have not made any disclosure on Steam as the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage. We are posting this disclosure as it has become a matter of public interest.

This is not an endorsement of, or argument for, the use of AI tools, however minimal. We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as “inevitable”. We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to videogames and our world, and apologise that Big Walk’s LLM usage may not meet their standards.

Big Walk was developed without an internal AI usage policy in place, and we consider that lack of policy a failure. We will work to have a more comprehensive policy going forwards."

As you can see, House House did not disclose its use of AI-generated code because "Steam as a platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage." It says it is posting the disclosure now as "it has become a matter of public interest."

House House recently made headlines for choosing not to put Big Walk on Xbox in accordance with the Palestinian-led BDS boycott against Microsoft Games. Earlier this year, it gained widespread critical acclaim for its unique emphasis on cooperative puzzle-solving – you can read more about that in Game Informer's Big Walk review.

#4140. Pikmin 4 Is Still Great, But Dandori Academy Is Underwhelming

Pikmin 4 was released for the original Switch in 2023, and it ranks among my favorite games on the platform; I happily award it the honor of being the best Pikmin game. It looks and plays great, and Oatchi the dog makes the sometimes annoying process of managing a collection of little plant creatures willing to do your bidding much smoother.

The over-titled Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy releases November 12, and much like other comparable Nintendo games that have been ported and improved for Switch 2 (like Kirby and Mario Party), the base game is as good as it was initially and looks even better. If you skipped Pikmin 4 on Switch for whatever reason (probably because it was day one of the Barbenheimer epidemic), I encourage you to play it now. You have about a week to beat it before… something else comes out. Who’s to say.

The “big” addition here for the Switch 2 version of the game, alongside improved performance and visuals and the ability to give Oatchi verbal commands, is Dandori Academy. The Academy is an expanded time trial mode that awards medals for practicing specific levels, which you can then play and upload your high scores on specific days. For example, I can play the Advanced B level, Rockaway Cellars, as much as I want, but it only really counts if I play it on November 12. And you only get one try (though you can unlock retry tickets).

In theory, I like the unique approach to high-score battling, and the limited timeframe adds fun intensity, but this isn't what I am looking for from Pikmin. I recognize and acknowledge the design decision to place timers on your interactions in Pikmin, but it’s never been my favorite part. I like building my adorable little army and exploring, discovering, and retrieving as many unexpected items as possible. But I mostly get annoyed at the ticking clock, especially when I am watching my crew meander toward my spaceship holding a Game Boy Advance SP (or whatever they manage to find on the never-acknowledged, but potentially post-apocalyptic Earth you are exploring).

I also like having a list of missions to complete, and in Dandori Academy, there isn’t much acknowledgment of your success in practice. You can earn a platinum medal while practicing Rockaway Cellar, but it’s mainly to let you know that this is what you could earn when you play on the right day.

The main takeaway is that Pikmin 4 is still excellent, and I was grateful to transfer my save file from the Switch version (and I was tempted to start a new game + save), but Dandori Academy is not a strong incentive to return if you already played the game. It is a nice bonus and an interesting concept that reimagines the familiar time trial mode featured in plenty of video games, but the original campaign is still the main attraction.

#4139. 10 Best Indie Video Game Boss Fights of 2026

Ronald is a video game journalist with more than 10 years of experience in the industry, working on several of the most important Spanish websites.

Year after year, indie video games constitute an increasingly significant portion of the best experiences the interactive medium has to offer, regardless of your favorite genre.

Whether you prefer horror, action-adventure, or RPGs, especially when it comes to niches like boss rushes or Metroidvanias, the ever-reliable indie developers are always ready to satisfy your gaming needs.

For the past couple of generations, I've personally focused more on these kinds of products than on big-budget blockbusters because I find them more exciting, which allows me to talk about them at length.

So, to start wrapping up the year and reflect on the great adventures we've enjoyed—and be warned that there will be spoilers for the games mentioned below—here are the ten best indie video game boss fights of 2026.

As a fan of games that simply throw memorable enemies at you with no filler in between, Gurei was one of my most pleasant surprises of 2026.

The idea of creating a boss rush where the foes vary in difficulty and complexity depending on the order in which you choose to face them, also affecting the abilities you have at your disposal, is fascinating, and this is most evident when you face the Beetle Kami.

This force of nature is an enjoyable fight, whether it's your first or last encounter, as it perfectly embodies the kind of battles that rely on learning precise movement patterns, leaving no room for error if you want to emerge victorious.

In all my Gurei runs, I rarely dared to leave the Beetle for last because the ability it gives you is powerful, but also because its difficulty spikes dramatically. In any case, it's clear that all his versions offer a satisfying clash between two honorable warriors, which is the best kind of duel.

Kernel Hearts is a game I admire more for its story and soundtrack than its gameplay. However, its bosses are the exception, especially thanks to the presence of entities like God.

Fighting at the edges of reality with an immortal being that constantly changes shape and name becomes fascinating in a matter of seconds, particularly because of its strange fighting style that perfectly explains why it's the deity of the game's world.

It's a grueling two-phase encounter that demands meticulous control of positioning and attack windows, all while avoiding beams of light, giant cubes, spiritual representations of your teammates, and the constant onslaught of its divine claws.

Like any good roguelike, the power level you reach when facing the final boss is what truly determines how much you'll suffer, but whether it's easy or difficult, God offers a magnificent fight.

As we approach the midway point of 2026, let's take a look at some under-the-radar indie gems that already feel like cult classic video games.

While Replaced didn't quite live up to my expectations, I wholeheartedly consider it among 2026's best action games, with The Commissioner being the greatest showcase of its precise gameplay.

Specifically, the second encounter with Cole Carpenter exploits all the title's mechanics to their fullest potential, forcing you to dodge, parry, and shoot as the situation demands in order to keep up with him.

The burning environment and tense soundtrack also perfectly complement the encounter, which highlights the magnificent animations and choreography that Replaced brings to its simple yet visually stunning combat system.

Overall, the game's roster of main enemies is good, but due to its narrative weight, audiovisual presentation, and elegant flow, The Commissioner is undoubtedly the most memorable one.

Well Dweller dedicates its entire campaign to pitting you against terrifyingly well-designed enemies in incredibly creative fights, eventually pairing you with The Queen so you can free your family (and the kingdom) from her yoke.

Striking the face of this abject royalty as you watch her gradually deform is a stunning sight, even when you're too busy dodging her countless projectiles to notice that you're slowly revealing her true form.

After hours of honing your skills and learning to maneuver Glimmer, Well Dweller tests your ability to jump, dodge, glide, and bounce without pausing for a second, forcing you to be so precise that you'll only succeed if you enter a state of flow.

Unlike the bosses in most modern Metroidvanias, which are heavily influenced by the Soulsborne philosophy, The Queen belongs to the more traditional action-platformer formula, and that makes her sensational.

Hack and slash games have been on the decline for many years, which is quite a shame for those of us who are fans of great fights, yet sporadically we get gems like SoulQuest that remind us of the genre's greatness.

Despite being conceptually simple, the way it adapts the gameplay style to two dimensions is compelling, as is the showdown against Morrigan, a feast of visual spectacle and stylized mechanics that fully exploit the title's strengths.

With all your combos and abilities unlocked, it's not just that you tackle a fast and multifaceted boss that attacks in numerous ways and directions, but also the fact that you can particularly counter them with a plethora of magnificent moves, fully settling the power fantasy.

Defeating a good boss is satisfying, but doing so with a deliberate use of interconnected attacks for diverse purposes to push your style metric to the limit is much more, so we have to thank SoulQuest for bringing back Devil May Cry's magic.

If you are feeling nostalgic, take a look at these 10 best boss fights of the PS1 era.

Never underestimate how much an excellent presentation can elevate the experience of a boss fight, especially when you have examples like the final encounter with Dolores in Crisol: Theater of Idols.

Thanks to her stunning art design, fighting her leaves you completely captivated, but even more so when you notice the Resident Evil inspiration behind the encounter, based on methodical positioning and remarkable aim to target her weak points.

Furthermore, the emotional component also plays a significant role because, without going into detail to avoid spoilers, the dialogues that unfold during the confrontation are heartbreaking, providing a powerful conclusion to the game's compelling story.

Crisol: Theater of Idols perfectly captures the essence of the genre's greats while forging its own unique identity, and it's impossible to finish the campaign with this fight and not be convinced of its remarkable quality.

Future Knight is, without a doubt, among the most original experiences I've had in 2026, and the fight against the Lady from the Past is just the icing on the cake of a game that only needs three hours to win you over.

Although all the bosses are bizarre and incredibly fun in their own way, finally facing the leader of the cult that brainwashed the world is special thanks to all the layers of the skirmish.

Facing an elderly woman who throws bombs from her hands, summons tiny old men who shoot everywhere, hurls flying underwear at you, and fires glitched paintings while distracting you by counting sheep is not the kind of memory that fades easily.

The secret boss in Future Knight would also be a strong contender for this distinction, though I'm sticking with the Lady from the Past because I still laugh when I think about her, thanks to how improbably entertaining the fight was.

One of the main reasons I believe MIO: Memories in Orbit belongs on the list of the best Metroidvanias of all time is its roster of bosses, with Shii leading the pack due to everything that her encounter entails.

The final challenge that separates you from the true finale is precisely the entity that has accompanied you throughout the journey, proving to be an incredibly powerful being that perfectly showcases the game's dynamic approach to boss fights.

Between its teleportations, position changes, rapid charges, variety of attacks, and diverse projectiles, it's a clash that compels you to use every tool at your disposal, making positioning just as crucial as knowing when to dodge.

If you add to that the ending it gives you access to, the lore of its background, and the remarkable soundtrack that accompanies it, Shii becomes the ultimate icon of MIO: Memories in Orbit, which is saying a lot considering the existence of fights like those of Ati, Sol & Vin, and Nabuu.

These 10 Easy But Impactful Boss Fights prove that challenging encounters aren't always needed to be a memorable boss

Boss fights in horror games are highly functional but also linear in their execution, unless your name is Tenebris Somnia and you deliver a confrontation as impressive as Lacuna's.

All the bosses in the game boast incredible design, both in pixel art and FMV, but this one in particular is a string of gameplay and visual surprises that keep you amazed until the very last second.

Honestly, I want to keep descriptions to a minimum to preserve the element of surprise, yet I will say that it's among the most incredible bosses in the entire genre for how it uses the environment, story, and mechanics to create a sense of being in front of an actual supernatural force.

It's true that combat isn't Tenebris Somnia's strong suit, but bosses like Lacuna know how to overcome limitations and turn their simplicity into a strength, as it allows you to focus on the fight's terrifying and immersive exhibition.

Mina the Hollower is a game that will surely be remembered as one of the finest in the entire indie scene of this decade, as it exudes such generational quality that every sequence is a masterpiece.

Nevertheless, facing Baron Lionel in his various forms is the campaign's clear highlight, boasting such inventive gameplay that you'll want to lose on purpose just to have another chance to fight him.

Whether in his standard form, which you face in the typical fashion the game has offered so far, or in his radiant form, which takes full advantage of the glorious tower-climbing mechanic to add verticality and perpetual movement to the fight, you'll be so satisfied that you won't want to fight any other boss for a good while.

Divine pixel art, superb music, an entire narrative sequence that defines the campaign's plot twist and reveals its treacherous nature, two independent phases that exploit the best of each of the game's gameplay facets... Yes, Baron Lionel is the whole package, and perhaps even more.

Thus, the most villainous villain in Mina the Hollower stands as the best indie video game boss fight of 2026, as it is also the best written, the best presented, and the best visualized of all the contenders.

If you want to catch up on the best releases of the year so far, I recommend the ten best indie games of 2026 (so far).
